cleanIntro: The BANISH 410 is a 3D-printed titanium suppressor for .410-bore shotguns. It attaches through a choke mount made for your shotgun and carries its own choke tube in the muzzle end. BANISH says plainly that it is not designed to be fully disassembled: the baffles do not come out, and only the mount interface and the chokes can be removed. Its whole service is a 24-hour soak, a brass brush in the blast chamber and a thorough clean of every thread, every 50 to 100 rounds. Everything about unloading your shotgun comes from that shotgun's own manual.

steps.title: Shotgun unloaded, action open and visibly clear
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the shotgun and open the action so you can see there is no ammunition in it. BANISH does not print a clearing procedure for your shotgun. It sends you to that gun's own manual, a licensed dealer or the gun's maker if you are not sure how.
steps.prose: A suppressed shotgun is quieter, not safer. Treat it exactly as you would the same gun without the can.
steps.quote: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.

steps.title: What it is rated for: .410 shotshells, with three exceptions
steps.action: Check what the can has been fed. It takes .410-bore shotshells from #8 through #2 shot, BB, BBB, 00 buck and slugs, in lead, steel, bismuth or tungsten. Not compatible: shells with non-typical wads, slugs without wads or rifled slugs, and steel or tungsten shot through a full choke.
steps.prose: Know which choke is in the can before you judge a load: steel and tungsten are listed as fine, but not with the Full. If it has been fed something on the list of exceptions, call BANISH before you fire it again.
steps.aside: Compatible with all .410 bore shotshell ammo from #8 shot through #2 shot, BB, BBB, 00 buck and slugs*
steps.quote: *Non-compatible ammunition - Shotgun shells with non-typical wad types - Slugs without wads / rifled slugs - No steel or tungsten shot when using full chokes
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: The can may still be hot after firing. Wait for it to cool, or use a suppressor cover or gloves, before you take hold of it.
steps.prose: Grabbing a hot can and twisting is how people get burned, and how a joint gets rushed.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use a suppressor cover (sold separately) or gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Hot after firing. Cover or gloves.

steps.title: Back off the collar and take the can off the choke mount
steps.action: With the shotgun clear and the can cool, loosen the collar of the choke mount and take the suppressor off the mount. The collar was tightened by hand and then with the supplied takedown wrench, so expect to need the wrench to start it.
steps.prose: BANISH prints how the can goes on and does not print a separate removal sequence; the collar is the joint it has you tighten last. If it will not start with the supplied wrench, stop and call BANISH rather than reach for a bigger tool.
steps.aside: Before cleaning, ensure the firearm is unloaded and remove the suppressor.
steps.quote: Tighten the collar of the choke mount to the suppressor. Use the supplied takedown wrench after hand tightening.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — MOUNTING THE SUPPRESSOR, step 4, p.4

steps.title: ⛔ Only the mount and the chokes come off — the baffles stay in
steps.action: The mount interface and the choke tubes are the only parts of the BANISH 410 that can be removed for cleaning. It is 3D-printed, it is not designed to be fully disassembled, and the baffles cannot come out. There is nothing past those two parts for you to open.
steps.prose: Anyone telling you to open it further is describing a different can. BANISH also says a 3D-printed suppressor cannot be repaired, so damage done trying to open it is not something that gets put right.
steps.quote: The additive-manufactured BANISH 410 is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface and chokes can be removed for cleaning.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — CLEANING, p.6

no.q: The additive-manufactured BANISH 410 is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface and chokes can be removed for cleaning.

steps.title: Twenty-four hour soak
steps.action: Put the whole can under cleaning solution, or seal the muzzle end and fill the inside, and leave it for 24 hours either way. Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or even dish soap all work. What does not is anything that strips the Cerakote.
steps.prose: The interval is every 50 to 100 rounds. Because the can never opens, the soak is what reaches the baffles, so do not cut it short.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50-100 rounds fired.
steps.quote: To clean, submerge the entire suppressor in cleaning solution. Or, seal the muzzle end of the suppressor and fill its interior with cleaning solution. In both cases, let the suppressor soak for 24 hours.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — CLEANING, p.6
steps.warn: Be sure not to use solutions that will strip the Cerakote finish.

steps.title: Brass brush the blast chamber
steps.action: After the soak, clean the blast chamber, the first chamber inside the mount end of the can, with a brass brush.
steps.prose: Brass is what BANISH names. The blast chamber is the only inside surface it has you brush, so leave the brush out of the baffles.
steps.quote: Once soaked, use a brass brush to clean the blast chamber.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Mount out, and every thread cleaned
steps.action: Take the mounting adapter out and clean all of the threads: the suppressor's own, and the mount's inside and outside threads. Clear out any debris or buildup. The choke tube in the muzzle end comes out too; the tools BANISH names for the mount and the choke are the supplied takedown wrench or a choke tool.
steps.prose: Carbon left in a thread is what stops the mount or the choke threading fully home. If a part will not move with the tools BANISH names, it goes to BANISH, not to pliers.
steps.aside: Use a choke tool or the supplied takedown wrench to thread the choke completely into the suppressor.
steps.quote: Remove the mounting adapter and thoroughly clean the threads, removing any debris or buildup. This includes the suppressor’s threads, as well as all internal and external mounting threads.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Let it dry, then put the mount back
steps.action: Let the suppressor dry before anything goes back in it. Then the choke mount is re-installed and the can goes back on the shotgun.
steps.prose: At the next range session, 10 to 15 clearing rounds blow out whatever the soak loosened.
steps.aside: During the next range session, fire 10-15 “clearing” rounds through the suppressor.
steps.quote: Once clean, allow the suppressor to dry. Re-install the choke mount and reattach to firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — CLEANING, p.6

steps.title: Protect the muzzle while the can is off
steps.action: Whenever the can is off the gun for storage or transport, protect the barrel's threads and crown with a thread protector or other muzzle device.
steps.prose: The choke mount screws into the barrel's muzzle, so a damaged thread there is what stops the mount going in straight next time.
steps.quote: Once the suppressor is removed from the host firearm, BANISH recommends using a thread protector or other muzzle device to protect the muzzle threads and crown during storage or transport.
steps.cite: BANISH 410 PRODUCT MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document (the maker's upload path is /2026/02/). — WARNING, p.2

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the mount interface and the chokes. On its CLEANING page (p.6) BANISH states: 'The additive-manufactured BANISH 410 is not designed to be fully disassembled and its baffles cannot be removed. Only the mount interface and chokes can be removed for cleaning.' It prints no procedure past those two parts, and the soak, the brass brush and the thread cleaning it does print are all in the routine lane above. Page 7 adds that 3D-printed suppressors cannot be repaired and asks the owner to contact BANISH before shipping one for repair. This listing therefore has no deep clean.

cleaning.name: INTERIOR
tasks: Whole can submerged, or muzzle end sealed and the inside filled, for 24 hours
Mild firearm solvent, sonic wash solution or dish soap
Blast chamber brushed with a brass brush after the soak
⛔ Never a solution that strips the Cerakote finish
⛔ Do not try to remove the baffles: they do not come out

cleaning.name: MOUNT, CHOKE & THREADS
tasks: Choke tube out of the muzzle end
Mount's inside and outside threads cleaned

cleaning.name: AFTER CLEANING
tasks: Suppressor dry before the choke mount goes back
10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session
Thread protector or other muzzle device on the barrel while the can is off

reassembly: Choke: select the one you want, insert it into the muzzle end of the suppressor and thread it in completely with a choke tool or the supplied takedown wrench.
Shotgun safe and unloaded before the mount goes on.
Insert the choke mount into the shotgun's barrel, then thread and tighten it with the takedown wrench or any choke tool.
Attach the suppressor to the choke mount.
Tighten the collar of the choke mount to the suppressor by hand, then with the supplied takedown wrench.
Refine the alignment and retighten as needed: your sight picture is unobstructed when you aim.
fncheck: With the shotgun still unloaded: the mount is fully seated in the barrel with no gap, the collar is tight, the choke is threaded completely in, the sight picture is unobstructed and nothing is blocking the can. ⛔ If there is any gap, do not fire with the suppressor attached. Check that it is still tight after the first 5 shots and every 30 after that, and fire 10-15 clearing rounds at the next range session. ⛔ No steel or tungsten shot through a full choke, no rifled slugs or slugs without wads, and no shells with non-typical wads. A 3D-printed can cannot be repaired: if it is damaged, contact BANISH Customer Service before you ship it.
